scope: RecoveryPanel/databases route and affected project environment maps, ordinary selectors, shell/client/status/date handling

findings.category: CWE-451: User Interface Misrepresentation of Critical Information
findings.evidence: apps/console/src/routes/projects.$projectId.tsx:91-97 renders every non-production/non-development kind as Aperçu and shows only generic environment.status, with no recoveryHold explanation at :113-120. database-profile-form.tsx:83-88 includes held recovery environments and labels them Aperçu; routes/access.tsx:147-149 includes them and labels every nonproduction kind Développement. infra-workload-form.tsx:77-89 translates recovery correctly but still offers held cells for ordinary application preparation. Independent render of the actual DatabaseProfileForm with a valid synthetic recovery environment produced mislabel=true and offered=true (artifacts/recovery-ui-selector-probe.cjs).
findings.refutation: The recovery panel itself correctly explains permanent HOLD and activation unavailable, and server-side normal provisioning/material guards deny held targets. Therefore this is not a backend isolation bypass. The project card/ordinary selectors are still real owner entry points for the new server-owned environment kind, and their labels imply preview/development behavior instead of the special held state.
findings.suggestion: Render a distinct French Restauration isolée card with recovery hold and activation unavailable, explicitly distinguishing a held preparation from physically verified paused restoration; point to real RecoveryPanel run state. Exclude or disable recoveryHold environments in ordinary database/access/application creation selectors. Keep allowed owner metadata edits.

verified.evidence: RecoveryPanel:102 and :182 key independent forms by selected source/backup and project/environment revisions. Controlled selections derive their corresponding projects/environments; submission takes FormData from that same keyed form and sends only bounded policy/registered IDs/current revisions. A removed/stale selection falls back to another ID and remounts the form.

RecoveryPanel:197 converts datetime-local input to ISO in the browser; input step=1 preserves seconds. Independent Europe/Paris evaluation of the production expression maps 2026-11-11T13:24:56 to 2026-11-11T12:24:56.000Z and back to local13:24:56. Display uses fr-FR local Intl.DateTimeFormat.

RecoveryPanel:48 restricts backup sources to ready allocations, :54-56 limits restores to healthy/restore-verified bounded intervals, :177/:251 disable absent source/backup actions, :309 disables admission without qualified execution. :81-91 preserves source/HOLD/all-service activation missing and no automatic scheduling claims. No activation/promote UI action exists.

Panel sends registered IDs/expected revisions/policy/hash/target/name only. Owner API/client parses versioned response contracts; generic backend errors translate through safe French messages. No SQL, repository path, source credentials, pgBackRest config/argv or private material is rendered.

Panel:296-300 labels unknown outcomes and retained reservations without automatic repeat. :329-365 displays actual archive/database and restore-verification timestamps and missing ancillary/effect/producer coverage separately. shared.tsx maps backup/archive/held-restore/stale states to French labels.

Viewed actual artifacts/recovery-desktop.png (1440px) and recovery-mobile.png (390px) returned by owner browser tests. Forms, French uncertainty/unavailable text and disabled recovery actions remain within panels without observed clipping or horizontal document overflow. The default configuration has no fabricated qualified source or successful restore.
